study.title: Bengaluru hard-rock two-aquifer over-exploited at 242%: scarce east quality exceedances and 82% deficit coverage
study.summary: NAQUIM 2.0 2023-25 maps 711 sq km Bengaluru hard-rock Peninsular Gneiss Closepet granite two-aquifer system desaturated weathered median 19.35 m and productive fractured 50-100 m 52% under 2676 vs 1893 MLD demand-supply 705 MLD losses 783 MLD tanker deficit. 2023 drought 686 mm 41 wells 4.1-85.5 pre 3.19-92.6 post 84% fall vs 2024 93 wells 2.51-163.51 pre 2.00-135.15 post 72% rise but deep outliers Gangappa -67.43 CAD +59.18 persist. DWLR 13 sites -0.932 to -4.346 m/yr 238 sq km east-southeast 52 wards scarce potentiometric 925-775 m amsl recharge >900 to discharge <825. Tritium 5 sites 3.77% granite 6.89% gneiss below GWRA. Quality nitrate 10-26% uranium 35-45% to 1109 ppb Mn 15-18% Se 12.5% F 12.64% Zn17302 Mn5000 Fe13024. LULC built 42-86% runoff 257.5-428.6 +66% recharge-worthy 356-68 174 floods +-20 mm/yr east subsidence infiltration 2.4-8.2. Plan lakes 2.97 desilt 8.30 BWSSB 2.20 parks 1.42 direct 14.89 plus Cauvery V 120.45 reuse 62 RWH 12.75 total 89.44 vs 108 deficit 82% at 242% exploited with 25 VES 198-ward AR and 12-well test evidence.

narrative.headline: GSI Campus EW deep fractured well

insights.explanation: Drilled 202.3 m with four zones at 21-22, 31-32, 115-116 and 195-196 mbgl, 3.75 lps and SWL 140.84 mbmp.
insights.title: Drilling and yield

insights.explanation: Red rose shows multiple NW-SE trends, near-perpendicular to OW-1 N-S and similar to OW-2, implying common source.
insights.title: Fracture orientation

limitations: Single campus cluster; SWL very deep relative to neighbours suggests compartmentalization.
narrative.summary: 202.3 m EW yielding 3.75 lps with deep 195-196 m zone and NW-SE fracture set.
narrative.visual_takeaway: Clustered campus point with deep SWL and multi-zone fractures.
narrative.why_it_matters: Tests deep fractured connectivity and anisotropy controlling local flow.

narrative.headline: GSI Campus OW-1 shallow-level observer

insights.explanation: Drilled 202.3 m with zones as printed 22-23 and 177-172 mbgl, 1.75 lps and shallow SWL 13.66 mbmp.
insights.title: Drilling and level contrast

insights.explanation: Green rose N-S trend interpreted to control shallow flow, perpendicular to EW/OW-2 set.
insights.title: Orientation control

limitations: Second fracture interval printed reversed 177-172; use as printed.
narrative.summary: 202.3 m OW-1 with 1.75 lps but shallow 13.66 mbmp and N-S fractures.
narrative.visual_takeaway: Neighbouring well with strikingly shallower level despite similar depth.
narrative.why_it_matters: Highlights compartmentalized shallow vs deep systems metres apart.

narrative.headline: GSI Campus OW-2 high-yield observer

insights.explanation: Drilled 200 m with zones 22-23, 113-114 and 195-196 mbgl, 7.45 lps highest of trio and SWL 111.82 mbmp.
insights.title: Best yield of cluster

insights.explanation: Blue rose similar to EW NW-SE, supporting common fracture source distinct from OW-1.
insights.title: Shared set with EW

limitations: Cluster-scale result; extrapolation beyond campus requires more wells.
narrative.summary: 200 m OW-2 yielding 7.45 lps from three zones with EW-like orientation.
narrative.visual_takeaway: Highest-discharge campus point linking 113 m and 195 m zones.
narrative.why_it_matters: Identifies productive deep fracture connectivity for targeted development.

observations.statement: System neutral buffered; high EC/TDS/TH from rock-water + anthropogenic; nitrate from sewage soak pits leachate dairy, remedy HDPE sewers Jakkur model RWH dilution + RO/IX; uranium geogenic oxidation UIV to UVI uranyl carbonate driven by dewatering, remedy RO/IX/EDR/MAR. Remediation guidance covers activated alumina adsorption with spent-media disposal, RO-reject ion-exchange for nitrates/uranium complexes, EDR for apartments, constructed reed-bed wetlands, and MAR with treated rainwater.

observations.statement: Strong EC-TDS, Cl-EC, EC-Na, TA-HCO3 correlations show same cations-anions, Cl+Na drive EC anthropogenic, alkalinity bicarbonate-dominated; weak Mg-SO4 silicate not gypsum, weak HCO3-Ca limited carbonate, zero nitrate/heavy-metal correlations localized sources; Chadha QI silicate weathering dominant with seasonal QII-QIV urban/reverse exchange shifts. Table 22 reports R2 bivariate correlations showing very strong EC-TDS and TA-HCO3, moderate TH-Ca/EC-Na, weak Mg-SO4/TH-Mg/SO4-NO3/Pb-Cu/Fe-Cu. Upper R2 correlation table reports low R2 (<0.2) for metal pairs and Cl-NO3 K-NO3 and Na_Cl_Ratio vs Cl, moderate to high for Na vs Cl, TDS vs Cl, EC vs SO4, Mg vs Ca, HCO3 vs Ca. Report interprets EC vs TDS strong correlation as general mineralization from same cations-anions and Cl vs EC strong correlation as chloride major contributor to EC of mostly anthropogenic source. Figure 60 Cl vs EC All Periods scatter with seasonal symbols and regressions shows R2 0.74 Pre_2023, 0.64 Post_2023, 0.47 Pre_2024, 0.75 Post_2024. Figure 61 EC vs Na All Periods R2 ranges 0.64-0.89 (text 0.639-0.887) indicating sodium major role in conductivity; TA vs HCO3 approximately 1 indicating alkalinity dominated by bicarbonate. observations.statement: Satellite InSAR confirms eastern-southeastern subsidence to +-20mm/yr linked to over-extraction deep levels, thick weak weathered Varthur-Whitefield, high-yield borewell dependence, partial piped cover, low <900mm rainfall; requires urgent management. Eastern zone deeper aquifer systems show high to very high yield potential >5 litres per second leading to heavy borewell abstraction for domestic, commercial and institutional use. Many eastern and peripheral wards are only partially covered by Cauvery piped water network causing heavy dependence on private borewells and groundwater stress. Decadal average annual rainfall in eastern parts is <900 mm/year, lower than western and southern zones; limited recharge plus high extraction exacerbates depletion and compaction. Correlation between land subsidence and hydrogeological stress is clearly evident in eastern Bengaluru city - Conclusions and Management Implications. observations.statement: Recommendations 1-4 for urban flood mitigation: increased extreme rainfall needs climate resilient infrastructure; dedicated storm water drains separate from sewage; Recharge the Rain where it falls (RR) roof-top harvesting; repair/renovation/rejuvenation including de-silting with proper inlet and outlet. Six major lakes/water bodies identified for repair, rejuvenation and de-silting: total water spread 666 ha in 2010 reduced to 382 ha in 2020, area to be reclaimed 284 ha, additional storage potential 284 ham considering minimum 1 m desilting; dual purpose of increasing groundwater recharge and reducing flood waters. Table row S.No.1: Name Varthur, Owner BDA, Water Spread area in 2010 177 ha, in 2020 110 ha, Area to be reclaimed 67 ha, Additional storage potential 67 ham. Table continuation rows 2-6 and Total: Bellandur (BDA) 284/144/140/140; Jakkur (BDA) 59/55/4/4; Hebbal (Forest Dept) 48/28/20/20; Doddabommasandra Lake (BBMP) 29/13/16/16; Kanaka Sarovara Lake (owner blank) 69/32/37/37; Total 666/382/284/284. Recommendation 6: identified encroached area 353.79 ha in 201 lakes under BBMP for priority removal; BBMP till Dec.2022 removed 8.60 ha; 111 DPRs (BBMP-109, BDA-02) for conservation/development of tanks passed by Technical Committee of KTCDA to be implemented on priority. Recommendations 7-11: traditional rajakaluves cascading lake system; additional lakes/ponds; SWD maintenance and anti-dumping laws; Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority Act 2014 to stop encroachment; BWSSB rainwater harvesting act 2009 amended 2021 and Section 72A obligation for 30'x40' (1200 sq ft) plots to reduce stress on storm water drains.

observations.statement: Groundwater potential zone mapping used integrated multi-criteria analysis of 6 thematic layers with AHP weightage and GIS overlay, subclass ranking 1-5 (Saaty 1980); Figure 74 reclassified into very high/high/moderate/low. Table 30 weightage: Geomorphology 40.8 (Valley fill Rank3 Overall122.449, Pediment Rank2 81.63265, Pediplain Rank2 81.63265, Water bodies Rank1 40.81633, Hills Rank1 40.81633); LULC 20.41 (Wastelands1/20.40816, Agricultural2/40.81633, Built up1/20.40816, Forest3/61.22449, Others2/40.81633, Water bodies2/40.81633); Lineament Density 13.61 (Very low1/13.60544, Low2/27.21088, Medium3/40.81633, High4/54.42177, Very high5/68.02721); Yield 10.2 (Low3/30.61224, Medium2/20.40816, High1/10.20408); Drainage density 8.11 (High1/8.163265, Medium2/16.32653, Low3/24.4898); Slope 6.81 (Very low4/27.21088, Low3/20.40816, Medium2/13.60544, High1/6.802721). Text (referring to Figure 73) describes four categories low/moderate/high/very high: large western/northwestern low potential due to limited aquifer, minimal weathering, hard rock and urbanization; moderate linear/patchy valley-fill; central/southern/eastern high to very high associated with fractures/lineaments/paleo-channels and better yield; eastern high aligns with land subsidence suggesting over-extraction contributing to instability; map for sustainable abstraction, recharge, monitoring.

observations.statement: Table 33 Highly Urbanized Areas: limited open space, high runoff from rooftops/paved surfaces; recommended Recharge Pits for houses/buildings, Recharge Wells next to borewells for direct aquifer injection, Percolation Trenches alongside roads/drains, Modular Rainwater Harvesting Tanks with overflow to recharge wells. Table 33 Semi-Urban and Transition Zones (moderate built-up, open land/campuses/parks) recommend Percolation Tanks, Recharge Shafts to penetrate low-permeability topsoil, Infiltration Basins; Peripheral and Peri-Urban Areas (significant open land, agricultural fields, traditional water bodies) recommend Farm Ponds dual use and Percolation Ponds larger community ponds desilted vegetated beds. Wards prioritized list in annexure-15; proposal for BBMP, BWSSB, KSPCB to adopt as groundwater management policy with recharge mandates in building by-laws and Smart City/AMRUT funds; objective decentralized artificial recharge across Bengaluru. Table 34 zone-wise: 1 Urban Core (High Density) Majestic/Koramangala/Indiranagar/Jayanagar/Malleshwaram/Yeshwantpur - Rooftop RWH with Pits, Recharge Wells beside Borewells, Percolation Trenches; 2 Semi-Urban Transition Yelahanka/HSR/Whitefield/Rajarajeshwari Nagar - Percolation Tanks, Recharge Shafts, Infiltration Basins; 3 Peripheral & Rural-Urban Anekal/Kanakapura Road/Varthur Outskirts - Farm Ponds & Percolation Ponds, Recharge Trenches. Implementation Roadmap: GIS/AHP mapping, awareness/training for engineers/RWAs, incentives (tax rebates, rainwater credits), PPP, IoT monitoring, adopt policy, by-laws/SWD mandates, Smart City/AMRUT budget; Key Challenge Limited Open Space with built-up land and concretized/encroached infiltration areas.

observations.statement: System neutral buffered; high EC/TDS/TH from rock-water + anthropogenic; nitrate from sewage soak pits leachate dairy, remedy HDPE sewers Jakkur model RWH dilution + RO/IX; uranium geogenic oxidation UIV to UVI uranyl carbonate driven by dewatering, remedy RO/IX/EDR/MAR. Remediation guidance covers activated alumina adsorption with spent-media disposal, RO-reject ion-exchange for nitrates/uranium complexes, EDR for apartments, constructed reed-bed wetlands, and MAR with treated rainwater.

observations.statement: Strong EC-TDS, Cl-EC, EC-Na, TA-HCO3 correlations show same cations-anions, Cl+Na drive EC anthropogenic, alkalinity bicarbonate-dominated; weak Mg-SO4 silicate not gypsum, weak HCO3-Ca limited carbonate, zero nitrate/heavy-metal correlations localized sources; Chadha QI silicate weathering dominant with seasonal QII-QIV urban/reverse exchange shifts. Table 22 reports R2 bivariate correlations showing very strong EC-TDS and TA-HCO3, moderate TH-Ca/EC-Na, weak Mg-SO4/TH-Mg/SO4-NO3/Pb-Cu/Fe-Cu. Upper R2 correlation table reports low R2 (<0.2) for metal pairs and Cl-NO3 K-NO3 and Na_Cl_Ratio vs Cl, moderate to high for Na vs Cl, TDS vs Cl, EC vs SO4, Mg vs Ca, HCO3 vs Ca. Report interprets EC vs TDS strong correlation as general mineralization from same cations-anions and Cl vs EC strong correlation as chloride major contributor to EC of mostly anthropogenic source. Figure 60 Cl vs EC All Periods scatter with seasonal symbols and regressions shows R2 0.74 Pre_2023, 0.64 Post_2023, 0.47 Pre_2024, 0.75 Post_2024. Figure 61 EC vs Na All Periods R2 ranges 0.64-0.89 (text 0.639-0.887) indicating sodium major role in conductivity; TA vs HCO3 approximately 1 indicating alkalinity dominated by bicarbonate. Weak correlations interpreted as Mg from silicate not gypsum, carbonate weathering not dominant in granitic terrain possibly supplemented by treated water NaOH, NO3-Cl K-NO3 near-zero random local sources, heavy metals localized contamination. Na/Cl ratio vs Cl low correlation R2 0.042-0.182 despite Na vs Cl strong correlation indicates varying additional input sources with fluctuating relative proportions while both increase together. Figure 62 Na_Cl_Ratio vs Cl scatter declining trend reports R2 0.17 Pre_2023, 0.18 Post_2023, 0.16 Pre_2024, 0.04 Post_2024.

observations.statement: 25 VES across GKVK, Koramangala, Whitefield, Banaswadi, Varthur, ISKON, Mallathalli, Haralur; topsoil thick east-mid-west, weathered thick >20-50m east/west/south, deep fractures >100m east/NE/SW aligned lineaments. VES 3-4 layers H/HA/AA/Q/QH/K/KH: topsoil 13.1-612 ohm-m 0.6-8.8m (Haralur lowest clayey, GKVK612 driest), weathered 17.1-110 ohm-m 8.6-100m (Haralur thinnest, MEG Quarter Guard thickest), fracture zones 50-200m listed; lake-bed clay at Haralur/ISKON; UI at 3 sites; litholog correlation V Valley-Sai Campus Nagasandra-BIEG good. Topsoil >2 m in eastern-middle-western parts non-uniform; <15 Ωm clayey versus higher resistivity dry soil. Eastern plus western southern areas weathered zone >20 m with patches >50 m interpreted as good aquifers for storage transmission recharge and well yields. Eastern NE SW parts have deeper fractures >100 mbgl 150-300 Ωm versus rest of city well correlated with lineaments dotted lines in Figure 65f; results in Table 25. Figure 65 six-panel interpolated maps (a)-(f) show resistivity and depth of topsoil weathered fractured zones across Bengaluru City outline with color scales 0-1000 Ωm 0-6 m 0-100 Ωm 0-60 m 100-400 Ωm 0-300 m.

observations.statement: Satellite InSAR confirms eastern-southeastern subsidence to +-20mm/yr linked to over-extraction deep levels, thick weak weathered Varthur-Whitefield, high-yield borewell dependence, partial piped cover, low <900mm rainfall; requires urgent management. Eastern zone deeper aquifer systems show high to very high yield potential >5 litres per second leading to heavy borewell abstraction for domestic, commercial and institutional use. Many eastern and peripheral wards are only partially covered by Cauvery piped water network causing heavy dependence on private borewells and groundwater stress. Decadal average annual rainfall in eastern parts is <900 mm/year, lower than western and southern zones; limited recharge plus high extraction exacerbates depletion and compaction. Correlation between land subsidence and hydrogeological stress is clearly evident in eastern Bengaluru city - Conclusions and Management Implications. Figure 66 composite links central subsidence velocity maps (a)VW (b)VH to: depth to weathered zone, post-monsoon 2024 depth to water level, decadal rainfall isohyets, Cauvery ward coverage, and deeper aquifer yield.

Annual post-monsoon 2023 to 2024 comparison shows uranium exceedance rise despite lower max, nitrate proportion improvement, manganese marginal decline, iron increase, total hardness slight rise.

Chadha interpretation: QI silicate weathering bicarbonate buffering dominates in granite gneiss; QII saline urban recharge; QIII salinization ion exchange; QIV bicarbonate in Na-rich water; pre-monsoon increase QIII+QIV evaporation usage; post-2023 QI+QIV recharge weathering; post-2024 dispersed rainfall recharge; seasonal dilution with pre-monsoon anthropogenic reverse exchange.

observations.statement: Recommendations 1-4 for urban flood mitigation: increased extreme rainfall needs climate resilient infrastructure; dedicated storm water drains separate from sewage; Recharge the Rain where it falls (RR) roof-top harvesting; repair/renovation/rejuvenation including de-silting with proper inlet and outlet. Six major lakes/water bodies identified for repair, rejuvenation and de-silting: total water spread 666 ha in 2010 reduced to 382 ha in 2020, area to be reclaimed 284 ha, additional storage potential 284 ham considering minimum 1 m desilting; dual purpose of increasing groundwater recharge and reducing flood waters. Table row S.No.1: Name Varthur, Owner BDA, Water Spread area in 2010 177 ha, in 2020 110 ha, Area to be reclaimed 67 ha, Additional storage potential 67 ham. Table continuation rows 2-6 and Total: Bellandur (BDA) 284/144/140/140; Jakkur (BDA) 59/55/4/4; Hebbal (Forest Dept) 48/28/20/20; Doddabommasandra Lake (BBMP) 29/13/16/16; Kanaka Sarovara Lake (owner blank) 69/32/37/37; Total 666/382/284/284. Recommendation 6: identified encroached area 353.79 ha in 201 lakes under BBMP for priority removal; BBMP till Dec.2022 removed 8.60 ha; 111 DPRs (BBMP-109, BDA-02) for conservation/development of tanks passed by Technical Committee of KTCDA to be implemented on priority. Recommendations 7-11: traditional rajakaluves cascading lake system; additional lakes/ponds; SWD maintenance and anti-dumping laws; Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority Act 2014 to stop encroachment; BWSSB rainwater harvesting act 2009 amended 2021 and Section 72A obligation for 30'x40' (1200 sq ft) plots to reduce stress on storm water drains.

observations.statement: Groundwater potential zone mapping used integrated multi-criteria analysis of 6 thematic layers with AHP weightage and GIS overlay, subclass ranking 1-5 (Saaty 1980); Figure 74 reclassified into very high/high/moderate/low. Table 30 weightage: Geomorphology 40.8 (Valley fill Rank3 Overall122.449, Pediment Rank2 81.63265, Pediplain Rank2 81.63265, Water bodies Rank1 40.81633, Hills Rank1 40.81633); LULC 20.41 (Wastelands1/20.40816, Agricultural2/40.81633, Built up1/20.40816, Forest3/61.22449, Others2/40.81633, Water bodies2/40.81633); Lineament Density 13.61 (Very low1/13.60544, Low2/27.21088, Medium3/40.81633, High4/54.42177, Very high5/68.02721); Yield 10.2 (Low3/30.61224, Medium2/20.40816, High1/10.20408); Drainage density 8.11 (High1/8.163265, Medium2/16.32653, Low3/24.4898); Slope 6.81 (Very low4/27.21088, Low3/20.40816, Medium2/13.60544, High1/6.802721). Text (referring to Figure 73) describes four categories low/moderate/high/very high: large western/northwestern low potential due to limited aquifer, minimal weathering, hard rock and urbanization; moderate linear/patchy valley-fill; central/southern/eastern high to very high associated with fractures/lineaments/paleo-channels and better yield; eastern high aligns with land subsidence suggesting over-extraction contributing to instability; map for sustainable abstraction, recharge, monitoring.

observations.statement: Table 33 Highly Urbanized Areas: limited open space, high runoff from rooftops/paved surfaces; recommended Recharge Pits for houses/buildings, Recharge Wells next to borewells for direct aquifer injection, Percolation Trenches alongside roads/drains, Modular Rainwater Harvesting Tanks with overflow to recharge wells. Table 33 Semi-Urban and Transition Zones (moderate built-up, open land/campuses/parks) recommend Percolation Tanks, Recharge Shafts to penetrate low-permeability topsoil, Infiltration Basins; Peripheral and Peri-Urban Areas (significant open land, agricultural fields, traditional water bodies) recommend Farm Ponds dual use and Percolation Ponds larger community ponds desilted vegetated beds. Wards prioritized list in annexure-15; proposal for BBMP, BWSSB, KSPCB to adopt as groundwater management policy with recharge mandates in building by-laws and Smart City/AMRUT funds; objective decentralized artificial recharge across Bengaluru. Table 34 zone-wise: 1 Urban Core (High Density) Majestic/Koramangala/Indiranagar/Jayanagar/Malleshwaram/Yeshwantpur - Rooftop RWH with Pits, Recharge Wells beside Borewells, Percolation Trenches; 2 Semi-Urban Transition Yelahanka/HSR/Whitefield/Rajarajeshwari Nagar - Percolation Tanks, Recharge Shafts, Infiltration Basins; 3 Peripheral & Rural-Urban Anekal/Kanakapura Road/Varthur Outskirts - Farm Ponds & Percolation Ponds, Recharge Trenches. Implementation Roadmap: GIS/AHP mapping, awareness/training for engineers/RWAs, incentives (tax rebates, rainwater credits), PPP, IoT monitoring, adopt policy, by-laws/SWD mandates, Smart City/AMRUT budget; Key Challenge Limited Open Space with built-up land and concretized/encroached infiltration areas.
